title: Implement Admin-bound lifecycle workflow and native system payment handoff
verify: The internal workflow accepts only fixed server-side entrypoints for native Admin events, re-reads the native order under lock, and updates merged lifecycle metadata.

Each pending order has one unpaid native system payment collection (`pp_system_default`); native Admin `paymentCollection.markAsPaid(...)` changes pending_payment to paid without deleting reservations or directly changing stock, and no external provider is called.
Native fulfillment-created, completed, unpaid-canceled, and confirmed-refund events project processing/completed/canceled/refunded through the same guards.
Late payment after expiry/cancellation, paid-order cancellation, contradictory source state, forged/missing Admin context, cross-order binding, and missing order fail closed with no mutation.
Duplicate event delivery is a safe no-op and does not emit duplicate lifecycle updates; FT-009 provider calls and FT-010 email side effects remain absent.
T3 verification records semantic-pass, HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done, and ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_NOTE: present.
evidence_required: Real local Medusa/PostgreSQL workflow evidence for payment, fulfillment, completion, cancel, refund, duplicate, and conflict cases.
Reservation counts/stock evidence proving payment preserves the hold and native fulfillment consumes it.
Sanitized logs and privacy scan with no provider payloads, credentials, cookies, tokens, PII, or production data.
Full T3 protocol, verify, semantic, checkpoint, and rollback/recovery evidence.
constraints: Use supported Medusa workflows/subscribers and the existing order lock; do not modify Medusa Core.
The current payment profile uses the installed native system provider only to create an unpaid collection that Admin can mark as paid; FT-009 remains a deferred provider profile.
Only native Admin session/RBAC actions may enter the private transition entrypoints; do not accept caller-supplied source, actor, order binding, or payment state.
Do not delete payment-success reservations, directly adjust inventory, auto-restock refunds, add a custom Admin route, or send emails.
invariants: Only current authoritative native state caused by an authenticated Admin action can advance the lifecycle.

Unpaid Admin cancellation persists the order as canceled, removes it from the active customer cart, releases the existing reservation through the supported cancel/expiry path, and cannot be reversed by a late event.
A payment-success transition preserves every native reservation until fulfillment.
Repeated events and retries cannot duplicate lifecycle metadata or cross a terminal state.
purpose: Connect native Medusa Admin operator events to one guarded, durable lifecycle transition boundary; keep the deferred FT-009 provider profile out of the current runtime.
success_outcome: Real local Medusa/PostgreSQL evidence shows correct lifecycle transitions, reservation safety, terminal guards, and idempotent repeats.
anti_goals: Do not implement YooKassa HTTP/webhook/authentication or email provider behavior.
Do not replace Medusa Admin, create an order read-model table, or change native inventory quantities directly.

forbidden_scope: FT-009 provider calls, webhook endpoint, credentials, replay ledger, return page
custom Admin or Store lifecycle API
Medusa Core source, production data, secrets, direct stock mutation
stop_conditions: Installed Medusa events or fulfillment workflow do not provide a truthful native handoff.
Payment-success reservation behavior cannot be proven without deleting or directly mutating stock.
A conflict requires changing FT-007 expiry semantics or FT-009 provider ownership.
Full T3 evidence cannot prove no mutation on rejected/duplicate events.
